articles.title: Bateman and Kirk hit homers to power Blue Jays to victory over Orioles
articles.summary: Brett Bateman and Alejandro Kirk homered to power the Toronto Blue Jays to a 7-3 victory over the Baltimore Orioles on Saturday at Rogers Centre. articles.title: 11 names added to MADD Ontario monument for impaired driving victims
articles.summary: Families of victims, community members, police officers and survivors of impaired driving gathered in Brampton Saturday for a ceremony, where 11 new names were added to an Ontario memorial that honours victims of alcohol and drug-involved crashes.

articles.title: Cyclists ride in opposition to Ford government’s plan to remove bike lanes
articles.summary: Premier Doug Ford’s bike lane removal and street reconfiguration plans may already be underway in Toronto but the battle over the future of cycling in the city continues. articles.title: President Donald Trump’s childhood home sells for $2 million
articles.summary: NEW YORK (AP) — Donald Trump's childhood home has sold for nearly $2 million after a renovation transformed the New York City residence from a mold-ridden cat den to a modern abode.

articles.title: Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei says AI industry needs to give safety measures time to catch up
articles.summary: NEW YORK (AP) — The CEO of Anthropic said Saturday the artificial-intelligence industry should slow its fast-moving development to give safety measures time to catch up. Without such a slowdown, Dario Amodei warned that within six to 12 months, AI could be capable of leading a swarm of agents that could take over the entire internet.

articles.title: ‘Elderly man’ rescued from midtown Toronto fire
articles.summary: Toronto police say an “elderly man” was rescued from a fire in midtown on Saturday morning. Emergency crews were called to the Davisville neighbourhood, near Millwood Road and Forman Avenue just before 10 a.m. Police say several homes were evacuated for safety. articles.summary: A man who is accused of selling dozens of fraudulent car insurance policies in the Greater Toronto Area has been charged. articles.title: Two uniforms, one deadly morning: A Mississauga firefighter and former soldier reflects on 9/11
articles.summary: Twenty-five years after the terror attacks of Sept. 11, 2001, Shawn Matheson recalls viewing them through two different lenses: as a firefighter in Mississauga, Ont., and as a Canadian reservist. The tragedy would take him to funerals at Ground Zero, foreshadow the war in Afghanistan and reveal the lasting emotional cost borne by soldiers and first responders alike.

articles.title: Reliance on visual inspections may have played role in GO train derailment at Union Station: report
articles.summary: A new report has found an overreliance on visual inspections of the train tracks may have contributed to the derailment of a GO Transit train at Toronto's Union Station that disrupted commuter travel for days earlier this year.

articles.title: Stellantis signs MOU with Canadian armoured vehicle maker on potential sale of Brampton, Ont., plant
articles.summary: Automaker Stellantis says it has signed a memorandum of understanding with Canadian armoured vehicle maker Roshel on a potential sale of its idled Brampton, Ont., assembly plant.

articles.title: 'Destruction is not necessary': Gardeners fight city plan to relocate 30-year-old community plot
articles.summary: A 30-year-old community garden in downtown Toronto will soon have to pull up its stakes and move, as the city prepares to transform a piece of land into an eight-storey supportive housing project.
